title: An in-place initializer after a dtype cast may not update the parameter
applies_when: Parameter or buffer initialization casts a tensor to a working dtype, applies an in-place initializer, and locally rebinds the result. Same-dtype tests may mask missing write-back.
lesson: Trace storage ownership, not just variable names. Tensor.to returns the original tensor when dtype and device already match, but a conversion creates another tensor. Preserve the destination and explicitly copy the initialized working-precision values back when the initialization contract permits it. Test FP16/BF16 alongside an FP32 control, destination storage identity, dtype, initialization gain, and the real constructor's initialization guards.
avoid_when: A functional initializer whose caller consumes its returned tensor may intentionally allocate. Do not blindly copy into loaded checkpoints, meta or distributed tensors, tied parameters, or autograd-tracked leaves. This lesson establishes an initialization hazard, not forward/kernel correctness or performance.

evidence.note: The API documents same-dtype/device self return and a new tensor for conversions; this explains why FP32-only tests can hide the storage hazard.
copy_ writes elements into the destination, including conversion from a different source dtype. Its use still requires the caller's initialization and autograd contract.
The proposed RWKV7 fix documents baseline low-precision failures, FP32 controls and CPU regression checks. Publication is not evidence of maintainer acceptance or GPU qualification.
Commit-pinned tests exercise tall/wide shapes, two gains, three dtypes, destination storage identity, real attention construction and preservation after repeated module initialization.
